summary: Full-extraction pass cbi-usa3 over 20 US documents. State Department Report of the Visa Office FY2019-FY2024: EB-5 Table V (visa numbers used, incl. adjustments of status) and Table VI (visas issued abroad), every foreign state of chargeability (zeros included), all class columns (C5/T5/I5/R5, and from FY2022 the non-reserved pool and rural / high-unemployment / infrastructure set-asides), region totals, dependent-area TOTALs and grand totals; all tables add up. Eight Federal Register documents (2019 modernization rule, 2023 Integrity Fund notice, 2024 USCIS fee rule, 2025 Gold Card order, 2025 EB-5 fee NPRM, 2026 I-140G notice, 2026 integrity NPRM, 2026 EB-5 fee final rule): receipts, forecasts, regional centers, site visits, investment and jobs, programme costs, fee terms and dated events. 18 new indicators proposed, mostly for regulatory-impact and small-entity statistics.

events.title: USCIS starts charging the USD 1,000 Integrity Fund fee on each regional-center investor petition
events.description: From 1 October 2022, following the Form I-526E filing instructions, USCIS collected a USD 1,000 EB-5 Integrity Fund fee with each new petition by a regional center investor (2022 Act, INA 203(b)(5)(J)(ii)(II)).
events.quote: Beginning on October 1, 2022 and in accordance with Form I–526E, Immigrant Petition by Regional Center Investor, filing instructions on the USCIS website, USCIS began collecting a $1,000 Integrity Fund Fee

events.title: USCIS defers the Integrity Fund late fee and sets terminations for non-payment from 31 May 2023
events.description: USCIS will not charge the late penalty fee until it sets its amount by further action, but will terminate the designation of a regional center that has not paid the full annual fee within 90 days of the due date; it will not start terminations before 31 May 2023, and in later years acts if the fee is unpaid by 31 December. It also sets how it counts "total investors" for the USD 20,000 / 10,000 tiers (I-526/I-526E petitions minus I-829 petitions filed).
events.location: PDF p. 3 (88 FR 13143), II.C Late Fee
events.quote: USCIS will maintain the statutory 90-day termination period and will not begin taking steps to terminate a regional center until May 31, 2023.

events.title: DHS proposes new EB-5 fee amounts (proposed, not adopted as proposed)
events.description: Proposed fees (Table 1): I-526 and I-526E initial USD 9,625 incl. a new USD 95 EB-5 technology fee (I-526E amendment 9,530); new Form I-527 (amendment to legacy I-526) 8,000; I-829 7,860; I-956 28,895 initial / 18,480 amendment; I-956F 29,935; I-956G 2,740; I-956H 55; I-956K 2,740 (current fees then 11,160 / 9,525 / 47,695 / 4,470 / none). Proposed amounts only: the final rule of 30 Sep 2026 set different fees. Note the RIA text (PDF p. 22) gives USD 44,600 and 28,525 for I-956 initial/amendment, inconsistent with Table 1.
events.quote: I–526E Immigrant Petition by Regional Center Investor—Amendment

events.title: DHS proposes inflation increase and late-payment penalties for EB-5 Integrity Fund fees (proposed)
events.description: Proposed +8.25% (CPI-U H1 2022 to H1 2024): I-526E Integrity Fund fee USD 1,000 to 1,085; regional center annual fee 10,000 to 10,825 and 20,000 to 21,650. Proposed penalties: 10% if paid on days 31-60, 20% on days 61-90, termination if unpaid after 90 days. The final rule adopted 10% (USD 1,100 / 11,000 / 22,000) and the penalties.
events.quote: the I–526E EB–5 Integrity Fund Fee of $1,000 would increase to $1,085; the $10,000 Regional Center Integrity Fund Fee would increase to $10,825; and the $20,000 Regional Center Integrity Fund Fee would increase to $21,650

events.title: Court dismisses regional centers' challenge to the Integrity Fund fee (S.D. Fla.)
events.description: Sunshine State Reg'l Ctr., Inc. v. Jaddou, 23-cv-60795 (S.D. Fla.): order granting DHS's motion to dismiss a suit arguing that regional centers designated before the 2022 Act need not pay the Integrity Fund fee; appeal filed Jan. 2024. Decision not retrieved.
events.quote: Sunshine State Reg'l Ctr., Inc. v. Jaddou, 23–cv–60795 (S.D. Fla. Dec. 29, 2023) (order granting DHS's motion to dismiss), appeal filed Jan. 1, 2024

events.title: Court dismisses second challenge to the Integrity Fund fee (D.D.C.)
events.description: EB5 Holdings, Inc. v. Jaddou, 23-cv-1180 (D.D.C.): order granting DHS's motion to dismiss, rejecting the argument that pre-2022 regional centers are exempt from the Integrity Fund fee. Decision not retrieved.
events.quote: EB5 Holdings, Inc. v. Jaddou, 23–cv–1180 (D.D.C. Feb. 20, 2024) (order granting DHS's motion to dismiss)

events.title: USCIS starts collecting the USD 1,000 Integrity Fund fee with Form I-526E
events.description: Each regional-center investor petition (Form I-526E) must pay USD 1,000 to the EB-5 Integrity Fund on top of the filing fee; DHS says collection began in 2022 (the annual regional center fee followed in March 2023).
events.quote: USCIS began collecting the new fee in 2022, as required by the EB–5 Reform Act.

events.title: USCIS publishes Form I-526E for regional-center investors
events.description: Form I-526E (Immigrant Petition by Regional Center Investor) was published on 1 June 2022 under the 2022 Act; Form I-526 is now for standalone investors.
events.quote: filed on or after June 1, 2022, the date USCIS published the form

events.title: Grace period for the stayed 2024 EB-5 fee amounts ends
events.description: After reinstating the pre-April 2024 EB-5 fees on 12 Nov 2025, USCIS accepted the previous (2024) fee amounts only for filings postmarked before 26 Nov 2025.
events.quote: USCIS informed the public that they would accept the previous fee for items postmarked before November 26, 2025.

events.title: Scheduled end of the reformed Regional Center Program authorisation
events.description: The 2022 Act authorises the reformed Regional Center Program from 14 May 2022 through 30 Sep 2027. DHS assumes Congress will extend it. Scheduled date, not an event that has happened.
events.quote: effective May 14, 2022, through September 30, 2027.

events.title: DHS seeks public input on reforming the Regional Center Program (advance notice)
events.description: DHS published an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (82 FR 3211) asking for input on reforming the Regional Center Program over fraud concerns; many of its questions were later settled by the 2022 Act.
events.quote: DHS published an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on January 11, 2017, seeking public input on a range of issues related to the Regional Center Program

events.title: Homeland Security Secretary tries to ratify the 2019 EB-5 Modernization rule
events.description: The Secretary attempted to ratify the 2019 rule on 31 March 2021; the court vacated it anyway on 22 June 2021. (Page 35 of the same document gives 26 March 2021 as the vacatur date, which conflicts with page 14.)
events.quote: Although the Secretary of Homeland Security attempted to ratify the EB–5 Modernization Rule on March 31, 2021, on June 22, 2021, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California vacated the rule

events.title: USCIS publishes Form I-956 for regional center designation
events.description: New Form I-956 replaced Form I-924; required for regional center designation from 14 May 2022, when the reformed program took effect.
events.quote: USCIS published Form I– 956 on May 13, 2022, under an exemption from the Paperwork Reduction Act

events.title: USCIS publishes project application and annual statement forms (I-956F, I-956G) and revises Form I-526
events.description: Form I-956F (project application) and Form I-956G (regional center annual statement, replacing I-924A) published on 1 June 2022; Form I-526 revised the same day. Table 6's note cites a USCIS release dated 2 June 2022.
events.quote: USCIS published Form I–956F on June 1, 2022

events.title: Site visit required before deciding post-2022 regional-center conditions-removal petitions
events.description: From 15 March 2024 the 2022 Act requires USCIS to conduct a site visit to the new commercial enterprise or business location before adjudicating a petition to remove conditions based on a petition filed after the Act.
events.quote: on or after March 15, 2024, USCIS must conduct a site visit to the relevant new commercial enterprise or business location identified in the regional center application before adjudicating any associated petition to remove conditions

events.title: DHS proposes USD 1.4 million minimum investment in high-employment areas (proposed)
events.description: Proposed, not final: the proposed rule would codify the USD 1,050,000 standard and USD 800,000 TEA/infrastructure minimums and set USD 1,400,000 (133 percent of the standard amount, rounded up to the nearest USD 50,000) for investments in high-employment areas, adjusted every 5 years from 1 Jan 2027; the statute would allow up to three times the standard (USD 3,150,000).
events.quote: DHS is proposing to set the investment amount for an area of high employment at $1,400,000.

events.title: EB-5 minimum investment amounts due for first automatic inflation adjustment
events.description: Under the 2022 Act the USD 1,050,000 and USD 800,000 minimums adjust automatically on 1 January 2027 and every 5 years after, by CPI-U change since 1 January 2022, rounded down to the nearest USD 50,000; the reduced amount stays at 75 percent of the standard. Scheduled, not yet happened at publication.
events.quote: This amount will adjust automatically on January 1, 2027, and every 5 years thereafter

events.title: Regional Center Program authorised until 30 September 2027
events.description: The 2022 Act authorised immigrant visas for regional center investors through 30 September 2027.
events.quote: authorized the issuance of immigrant visas to investors participating in the program through September 30, 2027

events.title: INS publishes the first EB-5 regulations
events.description: The legacy INS issued the EB-5 regulations (8 CFR 204.6 and 216.6) in 1991, setting the TEA investment at 50 percent of the standard amount and delegating high-unemployment TEA designation to the states.
events.quote: These commenters referenced the issuance of the EB–5 regulations in 1991 where legacy INS previously decided to delegate the TEA designation process to the states

events.title: GAO attributes low EB-5 participation to pending regulations and other factors
events.description: GAO-05-256 ('Immigrant Investors: Small Number of Participants Attributed to Pending Regulations and Other Factors') cited an onerous application process, long adjudications and the suspension of processing of over 900 EB-5 cases, some dating to 1995.
events.quote: GAO, Immigrant Investors: Small Number of Participants Attributed to Pending Regulations and Other Factors, p.3 GAO–05–256 (Apr. 2005).

events.title: CIS Ombudsman issues EB-5 programme recommendations
events.description: The CIS Ombudsman found low utilisation 'principally caused by significant regulatory and administrative obstacles, as well as uncertainties that undermine investor and stakeholder confidence'.
events.quote: CIS Ombudsman, Employment Creation Immigrant Visa (EB–5) Program Recommendations, March 18, 2009

events.title: Annual EB-5 visa cap reached for the first time (FY2014)
events.description: According to DHS (2014 Yearbook of Immigration Statistics, table 7), the annual EB-5 visa limit was reached for the first time in fiscal year 2014.
events.quote: The annual EB–5 visa cap was reached for the first time in fiscal year 2014.

events.title: State Department starts an EB-5 waiting list for mainland China
events.description: The May 2015 Visa Bulletin made EB-5 visas available to mainland-China-born investors only with priority dates before 1 May 2013. By the December 2018 Visa Bulletin the cut-off was 22 Aug 2014, a wait of over 40 months.
events.quote: In May 2015, the State Department found it necessary to establish a waiting list for petitioners with approved petitions born in mainland China

events.title: GAO reports on EB-5 project investments in targeted employment areas
events.description: GAO-16-749R: in a sample of Q4 FY2015 petitions, about 97% of TEA investors chose high-unemployment areas, 90% of those relied on combined census tracts, and only 12% invested in tracts with unemployment above 8%.
events.quote: GAO, Immigrant Investor Program: Proposed Project Investments in Targeted Employment Areas, GAO–16–749R, Published Sept. 19, 2016

events.title: USCIS 2016 comprehensive fee rule takes effect
events.description: The DHS fee rule 81 FR 73292 took effect on 23 Dec 2016; DHS ran a small-entity analysis of EB-5 regional centers for it. This document does not give the EB-5 fee amounts it set.
events.quote: the 2016 comprehensive fee rule, which went into effect on December 23, 2016. See 81 FR 73292.

events.title: DHS asks for input on Regional Center Program reform (advance notice)
events.description: Advance notice of proposed rulemaking, EB-5 Immigrant Investor Regional Center Program (82 FR 3211), on issues such as material change and mandatory exemplar filings. Not a rule.
events.quote: was published on January 11, 2017 at 82 FR 3211.

events.title: DHS proposes raising EB-5 minimum investment to USD 1.8 million / 1.35 million (proposed)
events.description: Proposed rule (82 FR 4738): standard amount USD 1.8 million, TEA amount USD 1.35 million (75 percent of standard, cutting the TEA discount to 25 percent), five-yearly CPI-U adjustment, DHS designation of high-unemployment TEAs, priority-date retention. Proposed only; 849 comments in an 89-day comment period. The final rule kept the TEA amount at 50 percent (USD 900,000).
events.quote: published in the Federal Register on January 13, 2017. See EB–5 Immigrant Investor Program Modernization; Proposed Rule, 82 FR 4738.

events.title: DHS publishes the EB-5 Modernization final rule
events.description: Final rule (84 FR 35750) published 24 Jul 2019, effective 21 Nov 2019. The USD 1.8 million standard amount adjusts USD 1,000,000 (1990) by CPI-U 130.7 (1990) to 237.017 (2015), about 81.34 percent, rounded; adjustments every five years from 1 Oct 2024, rounded down to the nearest USD 100,000, always measured from the 1990 amount; TEA amount 50 percent of standard; high-employment amount also USD 1.8 million (the statute would allow up to three times the standard, USD 5.4 million, never used). Vacated 22 June 2021.
events.quote: was 130.7 in 1990 and 237.017 in 2015. The actual increase in prices for the period was approximately 81.34 percent

events.title: DHS proposes new USCIS fee schedule incl. higher EB-5 fees (proposed)
events.description: Proposed rule 88 FR 402. Proposed fees (Table 1 'NPRM Fee(s)' column of the final rule): I-526/I-526E USD 11,160 (from 3,675), I-829 9,525 (from 3,750), I-956 and I-956F 47,695 (from 17,795), I-956G 4,470 (from 3,035). Finalised unchanged for these forms on 31 Jan 2024, effective 1 Apr 2024.
events.location: PDF p. 1 (89 FR 6194), Summary; Table 1 on PDF pp. 7, 9, 10
events.quote: This final rule also responds to public comments received on the USCIS proposed fee schedule published on January 4, 2023.

new_indicators.name: Programme filings received (all or other forms)
new_indicators.definition: Filings received (or forecast) in a period under a programme's forms other than the main investor petition and the petition to remove conditions: project/investment approval applications, intermediary annual statements, bona fides attestations, promoter registrations, petition amendments, or all programme forms together. Use breakdown form= for the form; empty breakdown = the source's all-form total.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 for the EB-5 fee rules (Forms I-527, I-956F, I-956G, I-956H, I-956K and all-form totals). Investor petitions stay in applications_received, I-829 in conditions_removal_petitions_received, I-956 in regional_center_applications_received.

new_indicators.name: Adjudication hours per decided case (completion rate)
new_indicators.definition: Average staff "touch time" in hours needed to decide one request of a given type, as estimated by the programme authority for fee setting or staffing. Not the time applicants wait (see processing_time_months).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (USCIS completion rates in the EB-5 fee rules). Use breakdown form=.

new_indicators.name: Processing time goal
new_indicators.definition: Target average time, in days, set in law or by the authority for deciding a type of application (a goal, not a measured time). Status budget.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (sec. 106(b) of the US EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022). Use breakdown form=.

new_indicators.name: Staff working on a programme
new_indicators.definition: Staff (full-time equivalents) assigned to, or planned for, administering an investment-migration programme at a date or for a period; notes say whether existing or additional positions. Use breakdown category= for the office.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (additional FTEs in the USCIS EB-5 fee study).

new_indicators.name: Investment-pooling entities that paid the annual programme fee
new_indicators.definition: Number of intermediary entities (e.g. US EB-5 regional centers) that paid the programme's annual fee for a fiscal year (e.g. the EB-5 Integrity Fund fee).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3. A lower-bound proxy for active designated entities.

new_indicators.name: Estimated impact of a rule change on programme users
new_indicators.definition: Monetised impact of a regulatory change on a programme's filers as estimated in the regulator's impact analysis: costs to the public, or transfers such as the change in fees paid to the authority, over the stated period (cumulative) or per year (annual_average). Use breakdown category= for impact type and discount rate. Status projection. Also covers paperwork/compliance cost estimates (category=compliance_...) and total projected fee transfers (category=transfers_total_fees).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (regulatory impact analyses of the EB-5 fee rules).

new_indicators.name: Programme capital per project (distribution)
new_indicators.definition: Investor-programme capital (or total capital for blended projects) per investment project, as a distribution statistic (median, mean, maximum) over the projects in the source's sample. Not a total.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (DHS small-entity analysis, 1,402 EB-5 projects FY 2018-2022).

new_indicators.name: Qualifying investments made (count)
new_indicators.definition: Number of qualifying investments made by programme investors in a period (about one per investor petition), as counted by the authority. Use breakdown route= and category= (e.g. reduced_amount).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (USCIS counts of regional-center investments FY 2016-2021 and FY 2016-2025).

new_indicators.name: Revenue of programme businesses (distribution)
new_indicators.definition: Revenue or estimated income of businesses involved in a programme (intermediaries such as EB-5 regional centers, or project companies such as new commercial enterprises and job-creating entities), as a distribution statistic over the source's sample. Not a total. Use breakdown category= for entity type, sample and statistic.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (DHS small-entity analysis, commercial database matches). Differs from rbi_intermediary_income (programme-wide profit or income).

new_indicators.name: Compliance site visits to programme entities
new_indicators.definition: Site visits, inspections or virtual checks of programme intermediaries or investment projects (e.g. US EB-5 regional centers, new commercial enterprises, job-creating entities) conducted by the programme authority in a period; use breakdown category= for visit type or outcome and route= for regional center/standalone.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 for DHS EB-5 integrity NPRM (2026) Table 13 and text. Say in notes whether virtual checks are included.

new_indicators.name: Businesses receiving programme investment
new_indicators.definition: Number of businesses that receive investor capital under a residence- or citizenship-by-investment programme (e.g. US EB-5 new commercial enterprises and job-creating entities), at a date or approved in a period; use breakdown category= for the entity type. Intermediaries such as regional centers are counted in regional_centers_designated. Includes counts of new commercial enterprises referenced in petitions filed in a period and DHS forecasts (status projection).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 for DHS EB-5 integrity NPRM (2026).

new_indicators.name: People waiting for an investor visa number
new_indicators.definition: People (principal investors plus family members) in the queue for a programme's immigrant visa numbers at a date, as counted or estimated by the source. Use breakdown category= for the group (e.g. approved_petitions, pending_petitions_estimated); empty for the total.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (EB-5 Modernization rule 2019: 40,017 with approved petitions, ~73,000 incl. pending). Unlike petitions_approved_awaiting_visa it counts people, not petitions.

new_indicators.name: Family members per main applicant
new_indicators.definition: Average number of dependants (spouses, children) per main applicant granted status or a visa under a programme in a period, as computed by the source.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (EB-5: 1.81 derivatives per principal FY2014-2016).

new_indicators.name: Investors per pooled-investment entity
new_indicators.definition: Average or median number of programme investors per project, enterprise or intermediary (e.g. EB-5 new commercial enterprise or regional center), as computed by the source. breakdown category= names the entity and statistic. Also used for distribution statistics (min, max, mean, median) of investors per regional center from small-entity samples.

new_indicators.name: Programme money as share of project cost
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the total cost or capital of projects funded through an investor programme that comes from programme investors (e.g. EB-5 capital), as estimated by the source; notes say whether mean or median and which projects.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (GAO-16-749R via DHS: median 29%, mean 40%; DHS 2016 NCE sample: 40% RC, 50% standalone).

new_indicators.name: Growth in applications received
new_indicators.definition: Average annual percentage growth in applications received over a period, as stated or projected by the source (never calculated by us).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (USCIS VPC: 39% a year since FY2008; 3.3% projected).

new_indicators.name: Projected minimum investment amount
new_indicators.definition: A government projection of what a programme's minimum investment amount would be after future automatic (e.g. inflation) adjustments, under stated scenarios. Not a programme term in force.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (EB-5 Modernization rule Table 4).

new_indicators.name: Census tracts combined per targeted employment area
new_indicators.definition: Mean or median number of census tracts combined to form a high-unemployment targeted employment area in EB-5 petitions, as computed by the source from a sample. Use category= for the statistic and cohort.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-usa3 (DHS 2016 NCE sample: mean 16, median 7).
